stem: When light falls on a surface and bounces back, the process is called __________.
solution: Reflection is the bouncing back of light from a surface.

stem: The ray of light that falls on a reflecting surface is called the __________ ray.
solution: The incident ray is the ray of light striking the surface.

stem: The ray of light that bounces back from a reflecting surface is called the __________ ray.
solution: The reflected ray is the one that bounces off the surface.

stem: The line drawn perpendicular to the reflecting surface at the point of incidence is the __________.
solution: The normal is the perpendicular line at the point where the ray strikes the surface.

stem: According to the law of reflection, the angle of incidence is __________ the angle of reflection.
solution: The law of reflection states that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.

stem: The image formed by a plane mirror is __________.
options: virtual, erect and of the same size
solution: A plane mirror forms a virtual, erect image of the same size as the object.

stem: Reflection from a smooth surface that forms a clear image is called __________ reflection.
solution: Regular reflection from a smooth surface produces a clear image.

stem: Reflection from a rough surface that scatters light in many directions is called __________ reflection.
solution: Diffuse reflection scatters light, so no clear image is formed.

stem: A mirror curved inward like the inside of a spoon is a __________ mirror.
solution: A concave mirror has a reflecting surface that curves inward.

stem: A mirror curved outward like the back of a spoon is a __________ mirror.
solution: A convex mirror curves outward and its reflecting surface bulges towards the object.

stem: A concave mirror can form a __________ image when the object is far from it.
solution: For a distant object, a concave mirror forms a real, inverted image.

stem: When an object is very close to a concave mirror, the image is __________.
solution: For an object very close (within the focus), a concave mirror gives a virtual, erect, enlarged image.

stem: A concave mirror is used as a __________ mirror because it can magnify.
solution: Concave mirrors magnify nearby objects, making them useful as shaving or make-up mirrors.

stem: A convex mirror always forms an image that is __________.
solution: A convex mirror always forms a diminished, erect, virtual image.

stem: Convex mirrors are used as rear-view mirrors in vehicles because they __________.
options: give a wider field of view
solution: Convex mirrors give a wider view of traffic behind, though the images are smaller.

stem: The bending of light as it passes from one transparent medium to another is called __________.
solution: Refraction is the bending of light when it travels from one medium to another.

stem: A pencil placed in a glass of water appears bent because of __________.
solution: Light bends (refracts) at the water surface, making the submerged part of the pencil look bent.

stem: Light bends towards the normal when it passes from a __________ medium to a denser medium.
solution: On entering a denser medium (e.g. air to water), light slows and bends towards the normal.

stem: A piece of transparent glass with curved surfaces used to bend light is called a __________.
solution: A lens is a transparent piece with curved surfaces that refracts light.

stem: A lens that is thicker in the middle than at the edges is a __________ lens.
solution: A convex lens is thicker in the middle and converges light.

stem: A lens that is thinner in the middle than at the edges is a __________ lens.
solution: A concave lens is thinner in the middle and diverges (spreads) light.

stem: A convex lens __________ a parallel beam of light.
solution: A convex lens converges parallel light rays to a focus.

stem: A concave lens __________ a parallel beam of light.
solution: A concave lens spreads out (diverges) parallel light rays.

stem: A convex lens used to magnify small objects is commonly called a __________.
solution: A convex lens acts as a magnifying glass, enlarging small nearby objects.

stem: A convex lens can form a real, inverted image when the object is __________ the lens.
solution: For a distant object, a convex lens forms a real, inverted image on a screen.

stem: A concave lens always forms an image that is __________.
solution: A concave lens always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image.

stem: White light passing through a prism splits into its component colours; this is called __________.
solution: Dispersion is the splitting of white light into its constituent colours by a prism.

stem: The band of seven colours obtained when white light is dispersed is called a __________.
solution: The spectrum is the band of colours produced by the dispersion of white light.

stem: A rainbow is formed by the __________ of sunlight by tiny water droplets.
solution: Raindrops disperse sunlight into its colours, forming a rainbow.

stem: The seven colours of the spectrum in order begin with red and end with __________.
solution: The spectrum runs red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet — ending in violet.

stem: The human eye focuses light onto a light-sensitive layer called the __________.
solution: The retina at the back of the eye is where the image forms and light is detected.

stem: The part of the eye that controls the amount of light entering it is the __________.
solution: The iris adjusts the size of the pupil, controlling the light entering the eye.

stem: The eye lens is a __________ lens that focuses light on the retina.
solution: The eye lens is a convex (converging) lens that focuses images on the retina.

stem: A person who cannot see distant objects clearly suffers from __________.
solution: In myopia, distant objects appear blurred; it is corrected with a concave lens.

stem: Short-sightedness (myopia) is corrected using a __________ lens.
solution: A concave lens diverges light so that distant objects focus correctly on the retina.

stem: Long-sightedness (hypermetropia), where nearby objects are blurred, is corrected using a __________ lens.
solution: A convex lens helps focus nearby objects on the retina, correcting hypermetropia.

stem: A real image can be __________, but a virtual image cannot.
solution: A real image can be caught on a screen, whereas a virtual image cannot.

stem: The image formed on the retina of the human eye is __________.
solution: The eye's convex lens forms a real, inverted image on the retina; the brain interprets it upright.

stem: A convex mirror is also called a __________ mirror.
solution: A convex mirror diverges reflected rays, so it is called a diverging mirror.

stem: A concave mirror is also called a __________ mirror.
solution: A concave mirror converges reflected rays, so it is called a converging mirror.

stem: Concave mirrors are used in torches and headlights to __________.
options: produce a parallel beam of light
solution: A bulb at the focus of a concave mirror produces a strong parallel beam of light.

stem: The speed of light is greatest in __________.
solution: Light travels fastest in vacuum (and nearly as fast in air); it slows in denser media.

stem: A magnifying glass forms an image that is __________ when the object is close to it.
solution: Held close to an object, a convex lens (magnifier) gives a virtual, erect, enlarged image.

stem: Light travels in __________ in a uniform medium.
solution: In a uniform medium, light travels in straight lines.

stem: A kaleidoscope works using the __________ of light between mirrors.
solution: A kaleidoscope produces patterns by multiple reflections between mirrors set at an angle.

stem: When light passes from water into air, it bends __________ the normal.
solution: Passing from a denser to a rarer medium, light bends away from the normal.

stem: A swimming pool looks shallower than it really is because of __________.
solution: Refraction bends light from the bottom, making the pool appear shallower than it is.

stem: Which mirror would give a police officer at a road junction the widest view of traffic?
solution: A convex mirror provides the widest field of view, useful at junctions.

stem: The main difference between a mirror and a lens is that a mirror works by __________ while a lens works by __________.
solution: Mirrors form images by reflecting light; lenses form images by refracting (bending) light.

stem: The central lesson of this chapter is that curved mirrors and lenses can form __________ images depending on the object's position.
solution: Curved mirrors and lenses form real or virtual, enlarged or diminished images depending on the setup.
